예루살렘에서의 체포와 바울의 변론: The arrest in Jerusalem and Paul's defense
- 수리아로 간다고 하는데 예루살렘까지 수리아령입니다. 예루살렘으로 간다:
- It says he's going to Syria, but everything down to Jerusalem was part of the Syrian province. So it means he's going to Jerusalem. You've all come to Chuncheon now, right? But for Eun-saem, who lives in Daejeon, it's correct to say she set out for Gangwon Province, and it's also correct to say she set out for Chuncheon.
- Now, the plan is to get on the ship tomorrow, but Paul hears that some of the Jews, having heard he's going to Jerusalem with a large sum of money, are planning to kill him. Paul is on his way with the offering he collected, so he's carrying a lot of money. So in the end he gives up on the ship and goes the long way around by land. Look at this map, everyone. By ship it's a quick trip, but going around by land like this would take more than 10 times as long, right?
 - The funny part is, who were the Jews who tried to kill Paul and take the money? People on their way to Jerusalem to worship. So since Paul has to go the long way anyway, he goes back around through the Macedonian region, and while he's at it he visits the churches he had planted and holds meetings, and that's how the third missionary journey begins. If he'd gone by ship, Acts would have ended at chapter 20, right?
4절에 보면 바울과 함께 가는 사람들 이름이 쭉 나와요. 이 사람들은 각: In verse 4 the names of the people going with Paul are all listed. These are representatives of each church. You can see Paul managing everything very transparently: guarding the money received as the offering, and making sure it's handled properly. He sends these people ahead to Troas. Now Paul's team moves in an organized way. They go ahead and get things ready, acting as staff so Paul can make full use of his time.
5절 끝에 보면 ‘우리’라는 말이 나오는데 지금 사도행전의 저자가 누가라: At the end of verse 5 the word 'us' appears - and who did we say the author of Acts is? Luke. Up to here Luke had been writing in the third person, but from here on he writes in the first person plural. So you can tell that from here on Luke was traveling with them.

<Acts 20:6> And we sailed away from ⑤ Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to ⑥ Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.

Last time he passed through Troas, they asked him to stay a while, but Paul couldn't find Titus and was anxious, so he just left, you know? To make up for disappointing them back then, he held meetings for seven days, and he went at it so passionately that it went on until Eutychus dozed off on the ledge, fell, and died. In the end Paul brings him back to life. It says the people were not a little comforted, right? The name Eutychus means 'fortunate.'

Look at verse 22. And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem - does he say he knows exactly what will happen to him there? No, he goes not knowing. The only thing the Holy Spirit tells him is that bonds and afflictions are waiting for him.

Even though bonds and afflictions are waiting, he doesn't count even his life dear when it comes to bearing witness to the gospel, and he goes. And in the second half of verse 25 he says, I know that ye all shall see my face no more - it seems he knows he's going to die. He's leaving the Ephesian elders words that are almost like a last will.
31. 3년이나 밤낮 없이 눈물로 훈계하던 것을 기억하라. 32. 지금: 31. Remember that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears. 32. <행21:15> 이 여러 날 후에 행장을 준비하여 ⑱예루살렘으로 올라갈새:

2. 예루살렘에서의 체포와 바울의 변론\n 1) 야고보의 제안(21:17:
2. The Arrest in Jerusalem and Paul's Defense
 1) James's proposal (21:17~21:25)
 - When he arrived in Jerusalem, he met James, Jesus' brother, and they talked about this and that,
 - and James proposed a kind of show: "Right now the Jews see you as someone who breaks the law. If people find out you've come, they'll cause an uproar, so take these four men who have made a vow, go through the purification rites with them, and pay their expenses. Then you'll look like someone who keeps the law in front of the Jews, so there won't be a problem."
 - Paul could have said, "Why should I?" but he does what James says.
 2) The uproar in the temple and Paul's arrest (21:26~22:29)
 - But people assumed Paul had brought Trophimus, the Greek he'd come with, into the temple, and the whole crowd rushed in, dragged Paul out of the temple, and beat him. Gentiles weren't allowed into the temple at all.
 - The commander hears about it and comes and arrests Paul, and they had beaten him so badly that verse 35 says he had to be carried. Paul asks the commander in Greek whether he may speak in his defense. "Canst thou speak Greek?" He was shocked. Even while being beaten to death, Paul is trying to preach. Honestly, this man Paul is crazy about the gospel.
그래서 허락을 받고 사람들을 손짓하여 조용히 시킨 다음에 히브리말로 연설: So he gets permission, motions with his hand to quiet the people, and starts his speech in Hebrew. Because he speaks in Hebrew, the people get even quieter. Well, the stage is set, so he just goes for it, starting from meeting the Lord on the road to Damascus and giving his whole testimony of everything since then, but look at verse 22. The people shout that he's not fit to live, he must be killed, and they throw off their clothes, throw dust in the air, and all chaos breaks loose.
천부장은 배신감 느끼죠. 혹시나 바울이 좀 변명을 해서 소요가 진정 될까: The commander feels betrayed. He'd hoped that maybe if Paul explained himself a bit, the riot would calm down, but it got even worse... So he says he'll get to the bottom of this even if he has to have him whipped, and when they tie him up with straps, Paul says just one thing: "Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?"
The centurion reports: "What are you going to do? This man is a Roman citizen..."
천부장이 “진짜 로마 시민이냐?”: The commander: "Are you really a Roman citizen?"
“나는 돈을 많이 주고 시민권을 샀다.”: "I paid a lot of money to buy my citizenship."
완전 KO죠? 심문하려던 사람들 도방가고 천부장도 결박한 것 때문에 두려:
A total knockout, right? The people who were going to interrogate him ran off, and the commander was afraid too, because he'd had him bound.
 3) Paul before the council (22:30~23:11)
 - With his feet now to the fire, the commander wants to find out what on earth the Jews are accusing Paul of, so he unties him, assembles the whole council, and has Paul speak before them. And here Paul uses his head. He talks about the resurrection, you know? The Sadducees always said there's no resurrection and the Pharisees said there is, and they fought like crazy over it, so when he touches exactly that issue, they end up fighting among themselves even more. Another uproar breaks out, and the commander, afraid Paul will get hurt, has him taken back into the barracks. This commander is really funny, isn't he?
<행23:11> 그 날 밤에 주께서 바울 곁에 서서 이르시되 담대하라 네: <Acts 23:11> And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
로마에서도 증거해야 한다는 말은 곧 로마 가는데 까지는 죽지 않는다는 보:
Saying he must bear witness in Rome too is a guarantee that he won't die until he gets to Rome, right?
4) The plot to kill Paul and his transfer to Caesarea (23:12~23:35)
 - At this point, Paul's nephew (his sister's son) learns that 40 men who vowed not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul are lying in ambush to kill him.  So Paul sends him to tell the commander. The commander sends 470 soldiers to Caesarea at 3 o'clock at night. Paul made good use of his Roman citizenship, didn't he?
 - When 40 people come out to kill Paul, God gets 470 people ready to protect him.
그래서 그 날 밤에 안디바드리(예루살렘과 가이사랴 사이)에 도착해서 다음:
So that night they reached Antipatris (between Jerusalem and Caesarea), and the next day they escorted Paul on to Governor Felix in Caesarea, and Felix kept him in Herod's palace.
 5) The defense before Felix (24:1~24:27)
 - Five days later the high priest Ananias and the lawyer Tertullus accuse Paul, and Paul defends himself once again.
22절. 총독 벨릭스가 예수를 아는 도를 조금 알고 있어서 심문을 연기해: Verse 22. Governor Felix knew a little about the Way of knowing Jesus, so he postpones the hearing. And he gives Paul some freedom and allows his friends to take care of him. A few days later Felix, together with his wife Drusilla, a Jewish woman, calls for Paul and hears about the faith in Jesus.
바울이 의와 절제와 장차 오는 심판을 가르치니까 두려워하면서도 또 혹 돈: When Paul teaches about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix is afraid, but he also keeps calling him in to talk, hoping Paul might give him some money. It's the same everywhere, isn't it?
<행24:27> 이태를 지내서 보르기오 베스도가 벨릭스의 소임을 대신하니:
<Acts 24:27> But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
 - So two years pass in the prison at Caesarea, and Paul gets time to calmly organize his theology, while Luke travels around Palestine collecting material to write the Gospel of Luke.
 6) The defense before Festus (25:1~12)
 - When Festus takes office, the Jews accuse Paul again and ask for him to be sent to Jerusalem. They planned to ambush him on the road and kill him. But Paul knows about the plot and says he appeals to Caesar and asks to be sent to Rome. A Roman citizen had the right to be tried in Rome.
 7) The defense before King Agrippa and Bernice (25:13~26:32)
 - A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice come to pay Festus a visit, and he says, "Good timing - let's hear what Paul has to say." Since he can't send him to Rome without any charge, it's partly to find out what the charges are, too.
 - Paul starts another long speech in front of King Agrippa, and partway through, listening,
베스도가 ‘니가 너무 많이 공부를 해서 미쳤다’: Festus says, 'You've studied so much that you've gone mad.'
아그립바 왕도 ‘너 나 전도하려고 그러는거지?’\n- 결국 자기들끼리 하:
And King Agrippa says, 'You're trying to evangelize me, aren't you?'
- In the end they say among themselves, 'He's done nothing worthy of death. If he hadn't appealed to Caesar, he could even have been set free...' Paul knows that too. But Paul's goal is to get to Rome, so since he's been accused anyway, he says, "Great. Now I can get all the way to Rome safely, for free!" and chooses to be tried before the emperor.
<행27:1~2> 우리의 배 타고 이달리야로 갈 일이 작정되매 바울과 다: <Acts 27:1~2> And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band. And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, (there was no direct ship, so for now they take a ship bound for Adramyttium.) we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
<행27:3~6> 이튿날 ①시돈에 대니 율리오가 바울을 친절히 하여 친구: <Acts 27:3~6> And the next day we touched at ① Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself. And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary. And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of ② Lycia. And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
<행27:7~8> 배가 더디 가 여러 날 만에 간신히 니도 맞은편에 이르: <Acts 27:7~8> And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone; And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called ③ The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
<행27:12> 그 항구가 과동(겨울나기)하기에 불편하므로 거기서 떠나:
<Acts 27:12> And because the haven was not commodious to winter in (to spend the winter), the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
 - At first a gentle south wind blows, so they think, great, and head toward Phoenix, but then a crazy wind called Euroclydon blows, and they can't get to Phoenix and get driven out to sea.
 - The reason the route went like this is that back then ships weren't engine-powered, they were sailing ships, so if a wave hit them broadside they'd capsize and that'd be the end; they had to turn the bow into the waves and cut through them. Just like a pirate-ship ride at an amusement park. So everyone was completely worn out. 276 people.
<행27:24~25> 바울아 두려워 말라 네가 가이사 앞에 서야 하겠고:
<Acts 27:24~25> Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee. Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
 -  He thought he might die too, but God had promised he would stand before Caesar, so he was bold. The ship might break apart, but the conclusion - that he'd get to Rome - was already settled, so he was calm. So Paul says, "We must be cast upon a certain island."
<행28:1> 우리가 구원을 얻은 후에 안즉 그 섬은 ④멜리데라 하더라\:
<Acts 28:1> And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called ④ Melita.
 - He stopped the sailors from running away, had everyone eat one last time, and gave thanks. In the end the ship broke apart, and everyone reached Malta and was saved.
 - On Malta Paul was bitten by a viper, and when he didn't die, the islanders thought he was a god; and then he healed the father of a man named Publius through prayer, so it turned into three months of meetings. Later, when Paul's group left, they loaded the ship with food for all 276 people.
<행28:11~15> 석 달 후에 그 섬에서 과동한 알렉산드리아 배를 우:
<Acts 28:11~15> And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux. And landing at ⑤ Syracuse, we tarried there three days. And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to ⑥ Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to ⑦ Puteoli: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward ⑧ Rome. And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns (three inns): whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
 - The Christians in Rome who heard that Paul had come all came out in a crowd and held a welcome ceremony. The centurion Julius, who had escorted him, was probably really shocked at this. What kind of man is this, that he's a prisoner and yet gets a welcome like this? How could he stay so calm when the sea was going crazy like that? On the island a viper bit him and he didn't die, and then the miracles of healing... anyway, through all of that, Julius probably wrote a good report about him.
<행28:30~31> 바울이 온 이태를 자기 셋집에 유하며 자기에게 오는:
<Acts 28:30~31> And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him, Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
 - Thanks to Julius's consideration, he didn't go to the jail for prisoners awaiting trial; he spent 2 years under house arrest in his own rented house until his verdict came. He didn't have freedom himself, but under this house arrest other people could come and go freely.
 - During this time Paul writes Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon, and Philippians, and because he wrote them in prison, they're called the Prison Epistles.
So now we're going to look at the four Prison Epistles.
